lane: Bibliography-support fetch for the Circle tweet's Wayback capture (bib key circle2023tweet)
target: Circle tweet "$3.3 billion of the ~$40 billion of USDC reserves remain at SVB" (@circle, posted approx. 10:11 PM ET, March 10, 2023); refs.bib already names capture timestamp 20230311032209

queries.query: exact-URL CDX, full history (no from/to bound)
queries.result: First row's timestamp (20230311032209) matches the capture refs.bib already names, confirming it is the first Wayback capture of this tweet URL. 58 total captures exist through 2025; one intervening capture (20230318065506) returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited by Twitter at crawl time), not used.

queries.query: snapshot fetch of the refs.bib-named capture (raw, id_ suffix)
queries.note: Wayback served this with Content-Encoding: gzip; fetched with curl --compressed to decode it, per the house pattern already documented in cdx_search_log.json (the circle2023update lane). Decoded HTML is Twitter's legacy server-rendered embed page (no live JS tweet body); the <title> element (built from HTML entities: ") decodes cleanly via BeautifulSoup to 'Circle on Twitter: "1/ Following the confirmation at the end of today that the wires initiated on Thursday to remove balances were not yet processed, $3.3 billion of the ~$40 billion of USDC reserves remain at SVB." / Twitter' -- an exact match to refs.bib's title field. The og:title/og:description meta tags carry the same text but with a leading tweet-thread-numeral glyph that decodes as a mis-encoded byte (renders as U+FFFD in this capture) -- the <title> tag was used as the verbatim extraction source instead since it round-trips cleanly through HTML-entity decoding and carries the identical wording.
